title: Compact DG bimodules with correct self extensions give fully faithful tensor
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Let $(A,d)$ and $(B,d)$ be such differential graded algebras. A differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodule $N$ has commuting unital graded left $A$- and right $B$-actions, with $d(an)=d(a)n+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(n)$ and $d(nb)=d(n)b+(-1)^{|n|}n\,d(b)$ for homogeneous elements. Use the derived tensor functor $T_N=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ of [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction]. Suppose that $N$ is compact in $D(B,d)$ [def-pc-compact-object], and for every $k\in\mathbf Z$ the map
$$H^k(A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(N,N[k])$$
induced by the left $A$-action is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Explicitly, a degree-$k$ cycle $a$ gives the degree-$k$ right $B$-linear map $n\mapsto an$, regarded as a map $N\to N[k]$, and its class depends only on $[a]$. Then $T_N:D(A,d)\to D(B,d)$ is fully faithful, meaning it induces a bijection on every morphism set. No generation assumption on $N$ is made.

proof.text: Put $T=T_N$ and $U=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(N,-)$. The specified adjunction gives exact functors $T\dashv U$ with shift-compatible unit $\eta$. The DG categories $D(A,d)$ and $D(B,d)$ are triangulated and have all small coproducts, represented by DG direct sums. As a left adjoint, $T$ preserves these coproducts. These are the categorical hypotheses needed below, with actual target $\mathcal T=D(B,d)$.

Each $A[k]$ is semi-free with the one-step filtration $0\subset A[k]$. The semi-free tensor computation therefore identifies $T(A[k])$ with $A[k]\otimes_A N$. The map $x\otimes n\mapsto xn$ identifies this DG $B$-module with $N[k]$; its inverse is $n\mapsto1\otimes n$. Balancing proves that they are inverse, and the differential on both sides is $(-1)^k d_N$ after this identification. For a cycle $a\in A^k$, the DG map $f_a:A\to A[k]$, $x\mapsto ax$, is sent by $T$ to $f_a\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$, hence to the map $N\to N[k]$, $n\mapsto an$. Thus the identification includes the specified action map on morphisms.

proof.text: For every $k$, the free-module formula identifies $H^k(A)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(A,A[k])$, taking $[a]$ to $f_a$. Under adjunction, postcomposition with $\eta_{A[k]}$ corresponds to applying $T$ to this morphism: naturality gives $\eta_{A[k]}f=UT(f)\eta_A$, which is the adjunction transpose of $T(f)$. By step 2 this is exactly the assumed isomorphism $H^k(A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(N,N[k])$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}(A,\eta_{A[k]})$ is bijective. Shift compatibility of the unit identifies it with $\operatorname{Hom}(A,\eta_A[k])$.

Choose a DG $A$-module representative $C$ for $UT(A)$. The shifted-free Hom formula at shift zero represents $\eta_A$ by a DG map $u:A\to C$. At every shift $k$, naturality of the free-module cohomology formula identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A,u[k])$ with $H^k(u)$. Step 3 makes all these maps bijective. Thus $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, which is inverted in $D(A,d)$ by its definition. Consequently $\eta_A$ is an isomorphism.

Apply the compact-unit propagation lemma to $T\dashv U$ and $\mathcal T=D(B,d)$. Step 1 supplies its exactness, shifts and coproduct hypotheses, step 2 gives $T(A)\cong N$, and step 4 gives the invertible unit at $A$. The assumed compactness of $N$ therefore gives its compactness hypothesis. Its conclusion is that every $\eta_M$ is invertible and $T_N$ is fully faithful. This lemma requires no generation of $D(B,d)$ by $N$, so no such assumption has entered the argument.

Step 5: lem-sfb-dg-adjunction-compact-unit, all hypotheses checked, T(A)=N compact.
